Subject: Request: Create private offer for Acme (pricing tiers + term options)

Hi —

We're preparing a private offer for Acme Corp (Account ID: 987654) and need help verifying Marketplace constraints. Summary:
- Offer: Redwood inference dedicated capacity + hosted API credits bundle.
- Two pricing tracks: 12-month term (standard discount) and 36-month amortized option (deeper discount).
- Need buyer approval flow: Acme requires a spot for Procurement to approve (procurement@acme.com) and Legal to accept EULA changes.

Questions:
1) Can AWS Marketplace support a private offer that presents both 12- and 36-month options to the buyer in the same offer ID, or should we create two separate offers?
2) Is there an AWS-side approval step we must trigger for multi-year billing schedule (annual upfront vs monthly amortization)?
3) Any known constraints on allowing a buyer-side contract amendment after the private offer is accepted (e.g., extension option)?

I've attached a one-pager and the pricing spreadsheet. Would appreciate a quick call tomorrow to sort the workflow; Acme wants to present to execs next week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: Create private offer for Acme (pricing tiers + term options)

Hi Vanessa / team —

Thanks for the details. Short answers below and happy to walk through live.

1) Marketplace handles private offers as discrete offer records per billing configuration. If you want both 12- and 36-month economics surfaced clearly to procurement, we recommend creating two offers and marking one as the preferred option in the cover note.

2) Multi-year billing is supported, but whether it requires AWS legal sign-off depends on payment terms (upfront annual vs monthly amortization). For monthly amortization that invoices through AWS, you should select the Marketplaces "Monthly" billing option and flag it for review. That will trigger a Marketplace Ops validation step.

3) Extensions/amendments are buyer-vendor agreements outside of Marketplace once the private offer executes. You can include a one-time extension option in the SOW and reference it in the offer note, but Marketplace won’t auto-apply an amendment — you’d need to issue a new private offer for the extension.

Next steps:
- Create two offer drafts (12m and 36m) and upload the SOW as an attachment on the offer.
- Choose billing schedule for the 36m option and mark it for ops review if amortized.
- Provide the buyer approval emails (procurement + legal) so Marketplace can add the correct approvers.

Sasha can help with the draft creation; Sasha — can you pick up the Offer templates for Acme?

Thanks,
AWS Marketplace PM
